post.caption: Micromosaic brooches hold thousands of glass tiles. Makers pull glass into thin threads called filati. They snap the threads into tiny pieces called tesserae. One small picture can hold hundreds or even thousands of pieces. Some of the tiny pieces are smaller than a pinhead. Workers set every piece one at a time with tweezers. The Vatican mosaic studio was officially established in 1727. A Roman doves mosaic found in 1737 became a favorite subject. Around 1775, Vatican trained makers led by Raffaelli began selling tiny mosaics. Grand Tour travelers bought micromosaic jewelry as souvenirs of Rome.
